PHP571 Methods in Epidemiology, Systematic Review, and Meta-Analysis.
This course introduces epidemiology, the study of health and disease in populations.
It emphasizes epidemiologic methods and research design for conducting and interpreting health research.
Additionally, the course will provide a detailed description of the systematic review process, discuss the strengths and limitations of the method, and provide step-by-step guidance on how to perform a systematic review and meta-analysis using statistical software.
PHP572 Measuring Outcomes and Identifying Causal Effects.
This course introduces students to the foundations of health outcome measurement and causal inference.
We will examine how clinical, humanistic, and economic outcomes, including patient-reported outcomes, are defined, measured, and validated, drawing on classical psychometric theory.

Students will also learn the potential outcomes framework for assessing whether interventions cause changes in health outcomes in both randomized trials and observational studies.
Examples from epidemiology and medical research will illustrate how accurate outcome measurement and rigorous causal reasoning support evidence-based decision-making in health care.
PHP670 Advanced Epidemiologic and Economic Methods in Health Sciences.
This course provides advanced training in pharmacoepidemiologic and pharmacoeconomic research methods and statistical analyses for evaluating health and cost outcomes, with emphasis on applied exercises utilizing contemporary approaches in the field.
Key aspects of the course include multivariable methods for common study designs, addressing bias, deriving and interpreting measures of effect, and economic modeling for assessing cost-effectiveness.
Course exercises utilize SAS and MS Excel to provide students with hands-on experience with various statistical models.

What are the program goals?
Goal 1: Graduates will be prepared to lead safety initiatives and programs for their organizations. 1.1 Operationalize a Safety Management Systems approach through an understanding of how technology, human performance, and organizational factors influence safety outcomes. 1.2 Communicate effectively the plans and methods for safety assessment and risk to non-safety educated leaders.
Goal 2: Graduates will have the technical skills necessary to understand and assess safety standards and practices. 2.1 Demonstrate strong fundamentals in statistics, data management, and safety performance indicators. 2.2 Apply hazard identification, risk assessment, and failure analysis tools including failure mode analysis, fault tree analysis, gap analysis and job task/hazard analysis.

Special Topics in Systems Safety (ISE 519 - permanent topics course): This permanent Special Topics course provides continuous, hands-on engagement through multiple 1-credit special problem experiences each semester, of which students may choose 4 total.

ISE 513: This course covers data management, methods, and sampling, along with identifying and tracking metrics such as key performance indicators and safety performance indicators.
Topics include DMAIC process, sampling, statistical process control and charts, process capability and limits, reliability analysis and regression, and forming arguments for safety systems.
ISE 515: Introduces risk assessment, failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA), lean manufacturing error proofing, product testing, and failure analysis.
The course requires applying complex models and techniques to real systems.

ISE/PSY 520: A study of human capabilities and their interactions with the systems where they perform their jobs to help engineers and psychologists to optimize design, improve jobs, and enhance system performance.
ISE 517: Introduces environmental health and safety practices and provides practical knowledge for risk management within various industries.
Students identify, evaluate, and assess control measures for hypothetical hazards.
ISE 518: Integrates engineering and management, enabling students to lead teams through change, communicate complex safety information, and interpret data-driven decisions for implementation of safety protocols and plans.
ISE 519: Special Topics in Systems Safety, such as Batteries, Wind Energy Safety, Solar Energy Safety, Marine Safety, Fire Safety, Construction Safety, Electrical Hazards, Petroleum Chemical Safety, and Transport Safety.
